According to al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), they must perform ritual washing after the cessation, as the reading with the doubled letter (*al-qira'ah bi-al-tashdid*, the recitation in which the letter is emphasized) makes clear, and as His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, indicates: ﴿When they have purified themselves﴾, for purifying oneself (*al-tatahhur*) is performing ritual washing. ﴿Then come to them from where Allah has commanded you.﴾ That is, from the place of approach which He has made lawful for you, namely the front passage (*al-qubul*). ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾, from what may perhaps occur from some of them in committing some of what they were forbidden, and from all other sins. ﴿And He loves those who purify themselves﴾, those who keep themselves far from indecencies and filth. The mention of repentance indicates that people have a real need for it, through some of them committing what they were forbidden (p-223). The repetition of the verb is for greater emphasis on the matter of purification.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 223:

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⦆; that is, places of tilling for you. They are likened to it because of the resemblance between what is cast into their wombs and seeds, in that each of the two is a substrate for what results from it. ﴿So go to your tilth⦆; when He described them as tilth, He described their intercourse as "going to" them. This explains His words (exalted is He): ﴿So go to them from where Allah has commanded you⦆.

﴿As you wish⦆: from whatever direction you wish. It is narrated that the Jews used to claim that whoever has intercourse with his wife from behind, in her front passage, his child will be born squint-eyed (ahwal). This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so this verse was revealed.

﴿And send forth for yourselves⦆; that is, what is stored up for you of reward. It has been said that it means seeking offspring; and it has been said that it means saying the name of Allah at the time of intercourse. ﴿And fear Allah⦆ by abstaining from His disobedience, of which is what has been mentioned among the matters. ﴿And know that you will meet Him⦆; so prepare yourselves for acquiring what will benefit you at that time, and avoid committing what will expose you to disgrace. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers⦆; those who receive what they have been addressed with of commands and prohibitions with good acceptance and compliance, with a reward of honour and everlasting bliss that explanation falls short of describing; or with every matter by which good tidings are given, things that gladden hearts and cool eyes. In this, along with the rhetorical effect of shifting the address and making the one giving the good tidings the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), there is an exaggerated honouring of the believers that is not hidden.

It is said: it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Rawahah, when he swore that he would not speak to his brother-in-law (khatn) Bashir ibn al-Nu'man, nor reconcile between him and his sister. It is also said: it was revealed concerning al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him), when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah, because of his involvement in the slander (hadith al-ifk).

"Al-'urdah" (عُرْضَةٌ) is of the pattern "fu'lah" in the sense of "maf'ul" (object), like "al-qubdah" (a handful) and "al-ghurfah" (a scoop). It is applied to that which lies across something and so becomes a barrier to it, as one says, "So-and-so is an 'urdah for good" (i.e., one who is set up for good), and to one who is exposed to a matter, as in the line of poetry:

*"So do not make me an 'urdah for the blamers."*

According to the first interpretation, the meaning is: do not make God a barrier against good matters that you swear to abandon. He is referred to by "oaths" because of their connection with them, as in the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to Abdullah ibn Samurah: "If you swear an oath and then see something else to be better than it, then do what is better and make expiation for your oath."

His (Exalted be He) statement, ﴿that you be righteous and God-fearing and make peace between people﴾, is either an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to "your oaths," or a substitute (badal) for it, since you know that the oaths are an expression for the matters sworn about. The lam in "li-aymanikum" is connected either to the verb, or to "'urdah," because of the meaning of obstruction it contains. That is: do not make God an obstacle to your righteousness, your God-fearing, and your reconciliation between people, by swearing by Him (Exalted be He) to abandon them. Or: do not make Him (Exalted be He) an 'urdah, that is, a thing that stands in the way of the aforementioned matters and blocks them, by means of the mentioned swearing by Him (Exalted be He) to abandon them.

It has been permitted that the lam be causal (li-l-ta'lil), and that "an tabarru..." etc. be connected to the verb or to "'urdah," in which case the oaths would be taken in their literal sense. You know well that this leads to separating the governing element (al-'amil) from its governed element (al-ma'mul) with a foreign element.

According to the second interpretation: do not make God a target for your oaths, which you cheapen by frequent swearing by Him. For this reason, the one concerning whom it was revealed, ﴿and do not obey every oft-swearing contemptible person﴾, is censured with the most grievous reproaches, and the "oft-swearing" (al-hallaf) is placed as its preface. "That you be righteous" then becomes a reason for the prohibition, that is: out of desire that you be righteous, God-fearing, and reconciling, because the oft-swearer is audacious toward God (Glorified be He), not reverent toward Him, and so he is not righteous, not God-fearing, and not trusted (thiqah) among people, and thus he is far removed from mediating in the reconciliation of relations between people. ﴿And God is All-Hearing﴾, who hears your oaths; ﴿All-Knowing﴾, who knows your intentions. So safeguard what you have been charged with.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 225:

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths﴾: al-laghw (what is "unintentional" or idle; literally, that which has fallen from the level of consideration) in speech is what has fallen away from the level of regard. Its meaning here, regarding oaths, is that to which there is no commitment and no intention; as indicated by His (Exalted) saying: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned in swearing oaths﴾ [or: "for the oaths you have firmly sworn"]; and this is what is meant by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾. This has been disputed. According to us (the Hanafis), it is that one swears to something he believes to be as he has sworn about, and then its opposite becomes apparent; there is no intention in it to lie. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, it is the saying of the Arabs: "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah," which they use to emphasize their speech, without the oath occurring to the mind. So the meaning on the first view is: Allah will not hold you accountable, i.e., will not punish you, for the idle oath that one of you swears while thinking that he is truthful in it; but He will punish you for what your hearts have committed of the sin of intending to lie in the oath; and that is in the case of the perjurious oath (al-ghamus). On the second view: He does not impose expiation upon you for what has no intention of swearing; but He imposes it upon you for what your hearts have intended and aimed at by the oath, and not merely what the tongue has earned. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾, in that He did not hold you accountable for the idle oath, although it arises from lack of deliberation and little care; ﴿Forbearing﴾, in that He did not hasten to punish. The clause is an interjected statement confirming the content of His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable﴾, etc. In it is an indication that what is meant by "holding accountable" is punishment, not the obligation of expiation; for expiation is what forgiveness and forbearance are related to, not the other way round.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 226:

﴿For those who take an oath to abstain from their wives﴾; al-iyla' (the oath of abstention, "ila'") is an oath; its proper construction is with "ʿalā" (on); its use with "min" (from) is due to its being made to imply the sense of distance; i.e., for those who swear while keeping away from their wives. It may also be that what is meant is: "for them, from their wives," like your saying: "I have from you such-and-such." It has also been read as "ālaw min nisāʾihim" (they swear off from their wives) and as "yuqsimūna min nisāʾihim" (they swear from their wives). The iyla' from a woman is that he says: "By Allah, I will not approach you for four months or more," on the restriction to months; or: "I will not approach you at all," and it does not apply to less than that. Its ruling is that if he returns to her within the period, by intercourse if that is possible, or by speech if he is unable to do so, the return (fa') is valid; and the one who is able to do so has broken his oath and is obligated to the expiation of the oath; there is no expiation for the one who is unable. And if the four months pass, she is separated by one irrevocable (ba'in) divorce. Al-tarabbus (waiting) means to wait and to hold off; it is attributed to the time period as an extension; i.e., they have the right to wait during this period without being pressed to either return (fay') or divorce. ﴿And if they return﴾; i.e., they go back on the oath by breaking it; the fa' here indicates detail, as when you say: "I am your guest this month; if I please you I will stay with you until its end, and if not, I will not stay except for as long as it takes me to move on." ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾; He forgives the one who swore the oath his return, which is like his repentance, the sin of breaking it, upon his making expiation; or what he intended by the iyla' of harm to the woman.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 227:

﴿And if they are resolved upon divorce﴾; and they have made up their minds to it; ﴿then indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾; of what has passed from them of the divorce, and of what is connected with it of grumbling (al-damdamah) and quarrelling (al-muqawalah) which the situation is customarily not free of; ﴿All-Knowing﴾; of their intentions. And in it is a warning against persistence (al-israr) and abandoning the return (al-fay'ah), which is not hidden.

(p-225) ﴿And the divorced women﴾: that is, those who have menstrual cycles, from among free women, who have been consummated with, since it has already been explained that there is no waiting period (ʿiddah) for a woman who has not been consummated with; and that the ʿiddah of a woman who does not menstruate, due to youth, old age, or pregnancy, is by months and by delivery of the child; and that the ʿiddah of a slave-woman is two qurū' or two months. ﴿They shall wait﴾: this is a statement with the meaning of a command, serving emphasis, by implying that what is commanded is something that must be received with haste in carrying it out, as if they had already complied with the command to wait, so it is reported as existing and realized. Its construction on the nominal form (mubtadaʾ) serves further emphasis. ﴿By themselves﴾: the bāʾ here indicates transitivity; that is, they restrain themselves and compel them to what they do not desire, rather it is hard upon them to wait. In this there is further urging for them to do so, because it indicates their being characterized by what they disdain, namely that their souls crave men, and this compels them to undertake what they have been commanded. ﴿Three qurū'﴾: it is in the accusative as an adverb of time or as an object, with an implied noun: that is, they shall wait for the duration of three qurū', or they shall wait for the passing of three qurū'. It is the plural of "qurʾ", and what is meant by it is menstruation (ḥayḍ), by the evidence of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Leave off prayer during the days of your qurū'," and his (ﷺ) saying: "The divorce of a slave-woman is two pronouncements, and her waiting period is two menstrual periods," and by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubts, their waiting period is three months﴾. Also, because the primary purpose of the ʿiddah is to establish that the womb is clear, and its basis is menstruation, not purity. It is said: "The woman has qurū'" when she menstruates. As for His (Exalted) saying: ﴿So divorce them for their waiting period﴾, its meaning is: beginning their waiting period; and it is the three menstrual periods. The use of the plural of abundance (jamʿ al-kathrah) in the place of the plural of paucity (jamʿ al-qillah) is by way of extension, since the substitution of each of the two plurals for the other is common and widespread. It was also read as "thalāthata quruwwin" without hamzah. ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾: of menstruation and of the child, out of haste to end the waiting period and to nullify the right of return (rajʿah). In this there is evidence that their word is accepted regarding that, both negation and affirmation. ﴿If they believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾: the response of the conditional is omitted, indicated clearly by what precedes it; that is: then let them not dare to do that, for the requirement of faith in Allah (Exalted) and the Last Day, on which reward and punishment occur, is definitely incompatible with it. ﴿And their husbands﴾: "bu'ūlah" is the plural of "baʿl", which originally means master and owner; the tāʾ is for the feminine form of the plural, as in "al-ḥuzūnah" and "al-suhūlah". Or it is a verbal noun, with an implied noun: that is, the people of their husbands, meaning their spouses, who divorced them with a revocable divorce, as the designation of them as "bu'ūlah" indicates. The pronoun refers to some of the individuals of the divorced women. ﴿Are more entitled to take them back﴾: to return them to their possession, by resumption (rajʿah) to them. ﴿In that﴾: that is, in the time of waiting. The form of comparison serves to indicate that if the man wishes resumption and the woman refuses it, his word is to be preferred over hers; not that she also has a right of resumption. ﴿If they desire﴾: that is, the husbands in resumption. ﴿Reconciliation﴾: between them and their wives, and kindness towards them, and they do not intend harm to them. The meaning is not that intending reconciliation is a condition for the validity of resumption; rather it is an exhortation to it and a prohibition against intending harm. ﴿And they (the women) have rights﴾: upon them, from among the rights, ﴿similar to that which﴾ they have ﴿upon them, according to what is customary﴾: from the rights which must be observed and whose preservation is obligatory. ﴿But men have a degree over them﴾: that is, an excess in right, because their rights over their persons are greater, while the women's rights are in the dowry (mahr), sustenance, avoiding harm, and the like; or it is a superiority in merit, because they are guardians over them (qawwāmūn), protectors of them, and because of what is in their hands; they share with them in what is the purpose of marriage, and they uniquely possess the excellence of care and provision. ﴿And Allah is Mighty﴾: able to take vengeance upon whoever opposes His rulings; ﴿Wise﴾: whose laws encompass wisdoms and benefits.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 229:**

﴿The divorce﴾: it means "al-tatliq" (the act of pronouncing divorce), like "al-salam" meaning "al-taslim" (greeting). What is intended is the revocable divorce (*raj'i*), because it is the one that precedes, and its ruling is the closest to what is mentioned, and because of what is narrated: "that he ﷺ was asked about the third (divorce), and he ﷺ said: 'Or release with good treatment.'" It is a subject (*mubtada'*) with an elided genitive modifier (*mudaf*) assumed, whose predicate (*khabar*) is what follows, that is: the number of divorces in which the husband has the right to return and to resume the marriage (*al-raj'ah*), as was explained just above. ﴿Twice﴾: that is, two. The choice of the form in which the noble text is expressed (*marratan*, "twice") rather than other forms is to indicate that their right is that they occur one after another, not all at once; although the ruling of return is established then too. ﴿Then retain﴾: that is, the ruling after the two is to retain them by taking them back (*bi-l-raj'ah*). ﴿In kindness﴾: that is, with good companionship and gentle treatment. ﴿Or release with goodness﴾: by the third pronouncement, as is narrated from him ﷺ; or by not returning until the waiting period (*'iddah*) ends, whereupon she becomes separated (*tabin*). It has also been said: what is intended is lawful divorce (*al-talaq al-shar'i*), and by "twice" is meant the general repetition, not the exact number two, as in His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Then return the gaze twice﴾, that is, a glance after another glance. The meaning is that lawful divorce is one pronouncement after another, in succession, not combining two or three pronouncements together; for that is an innovation (*bid'ah*) according to us. Then His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Then retain﴾, etc., is a ruling that begins a new sentence (*mubtada'*) and a resumed option (*takhyir mustanif*), and the *fa* in it indicates sequence following the instruction, as if it were said: "When you know the manner of pronouncing divorce, then your matter is one of two things."

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take﴾ from them, in exchange for the divorce, ﴿of what you have given them﴾: that is, of the dowries (*sadaqat*). Its specific mention, although the rest of their property shares in the ruling, is either to observe custom or to draw attention to the fact that if it is not lawful for them to take what they gave in exchange for intimacy (*al-bud'*) when it has left their possession, then it is all the more unlawful to take what has no connection to intimacy; and it is more fitting and more certain. ﴿Anything﴾: that is, even a small trifle, let alone a large amount. The placement of the adverbial phrase (*al-zarf*) before it is for a reason that has been mentioned many times. The address is to the rulers (*al-hukkam*), and the attribution of the taking and the giving to them is because they are the ones who command both at the time of litigation. It has been said that the address is to the husbands, and what follows is to the rulers; but that would disturb the noble wording according to the well-known reading.

﴿Except that they both fear﴾: that is, the spouses. It is also read as "yazunna" (they both suppose), and this supports interpreting "fear" as "supposition." ﴿That they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾: that is, that they will not observe the obligations of the rulings of marriage. It is also read as "yukhafa" (passive voice), with "an" (that) replacing its complement of the pronoun as a substitution of inclusion (*badal al-ishtimal*); and it is read as "takhafa" and "tuqima" with the second-person address.

﴿So if you fear﴾, O rulers, ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, that is, the spouses, ﴿by observing some signs and indications, ﴿then there is no blame upon them both﴾: that is, upon the two spouses ﴿concerning what she ransoms herself with﴾, not upon the husband for taking what she ransoms herself with, nor upon her for giving it to him. It is narrated that Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul used to hate her husband Thabit ibn Qays, so she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Neither I nor Thabit; by Allah, nothing will join my head and his. By Allah, I do not fault him in religion or character, but I dislike disbelief in Islam. I cannot bear him out of hatred. I lifted the side of the tent and saw him coming in a group, and he was the blackest of them, the shortest of them in stature, and the ugliest of them in face." So the verse was revealed, and she gave herself up to divorce (*khul'*) from him in exchange for a garden that he had given her as her dowry.

﴿Those﴾, that is, the rulings mentioned, ﴿are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ by opposing or abandoning them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾, that is, the transgressors, ﴿those﴾, the plural being in view of the meaning of the relative pronoun, ﴿are the wrongdoers﴾: that is, to their own selves, by exposing them to the wrath of Allah (exalted is He) and His punishment. The placement of the noble name (Allah) in the last three positions in place of the pronoun is to cultivate awe and to instill reverence; and following the prohibition with the threat is for emphasis in warning.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 230:

﴿Then if he divorces her﴾; i.e., after the two divorces; ﴿then she is not lawful﴾; she is not; ﴿to him thereafter﴾; i.e., after this divorce; ﴿until she marries another husband﴾; i.e., she marries someone other than him; (for nikah (marriage) is also attributed to each of the two, and whoever restricted it to the contract (al-'aqd) based his view on its apparent meaning; but the majority (al-jumhur) require consummation (al-isabah), on the basis of what is related that the wife of Rifa'ah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Rifa'ah divorced me, and his divorce of me was final; then 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr married me, and what is with him is like the fringe of a garment." He ﷺ said: "Do you want to return to Rifa'ah? No, not until you taste his honey (usaylah) and he tastes yours." And by a similar report it is permissible to add to the Book (al-ziyadah 'ala al-Kitab); and it has been said: nikah, in the sense of both "intercourse" (al-wat') and "the contract" (al-'aqd), is derived from the word "spouse" (al-zawj); and the wisdom behind this legislation is to deter hastening to divorce and to deter returning to a woman divorced three times, and to create desire for her. Marriage with the condition of making her lawful (tahlil) is disliked according to us; it is narrated that there is no dislike when the condition is not stated explicitly; and it is invalid according to most scholars, based on his ﷺ saying: "May Allah curse the one who makes lawful (al-muhallil) and the one for whom it is made lawful (al-muhallal lahu)."

﴿Then if he (the second husband) divorces her﴾; i.e., the second husband; ﴿there is no blame upon them both﴾; i.e., upon the first husband and the woman; ﴿for them to return to one another﴾; that each of them return to the other by contract; ﴿if they think that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾; which He has required them to observe as rights between the spouses. There is no basis for interpreting "thinking" (zann) as "knowing" (ilm), since outcomes are not known; and because "an" (that) in this construction governs an expectation that contradicts knowledge; for this reason one hardly says: "I know that Zayd will stand."

﴿And these﴾: a reference to the rulings mentioned up to this point; ﴿are the limits of Allah﴾; i.e., His specified rulings, protected from being violated by change or contravention; ﴿which He makes clear﴾; by this clear explanation; or He will make them clear in what follows, on the basis that some of them will receive further disclosure and explanation through the Book and the Sunnah. The clause is a second predicate, according to those who permit it to be a clause, as in His saying (Exalted): ﴿so behold, it was a moving serpent﴾; or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from "the limits of Allah," with the implied verb being the sense of the demonstrative; ﴿for a people who know﴾; i.e., who understand. Their specific mention, despite the generality of the call and the conveyance, is because they are the ones who benefit from the explanation; or because what will be added as explanation to some of the texts is not comprehended except by those firmly rooted in knowledge.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 231:**

﴿When you divorce women and they reach their term (ajal)﴾; i.e., the end of their waiting period ('idda). For the term (ajal), just as it applies to the duration, it applies to its end; and "reaching" (buluugh) is arriving at a thing, though it may be said of approaching it, by extension; and this is what is meant here, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿then retain them in kindness or release them in kindness﴾, since there is no place for retaining after the term has definitely been reached. That is: take them back without harm, or leave them until their term ends, in goodness, without prolonging it. This, as you see, is a repetition of the ruling in one of its forms, out of concern for its matter and as an emphasis on the obligation of observing it. ﴿And do not retain them to harm them﴾: a confirmation of the command to retain in kindness, a clarification of its meaning, and an explicit prohibition of what they used to practise. That is: do not take them back intending to harm them. The divorcer would leave the woman in her waiting period until, when she was about to finish the term, he would take her back, not out of desire for her but in order to prolong the waiting period for her. So he was forbidden from this, after being commanded to its opposite, for the reason mentioned. "Harm" (dirar) is in the accusative, either as a causative (illiyya) or as a circumstantial (haliyya) accusative; that is: do not retain them for the purpose of harming them, or while intending harm. The lam in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿so that you transgress﴾ is connected to "harm"; that is: so that you wrong them by compelling them to ransom themselves (ifida'). ﴿And whoever does that﴾; i.e., what was mentioned of retaining which leads to wrong; and the distance implied in the demonstrative serves to indicate the distance of his rank in evil and corruption. ﴿Then he has wronged himself﴾; within his wronging of them, by exposing himself to punishment. ﴿And do not take the signs of God﴾, which contain the rulings mentioned, or: all His signs, which fall within them in the first place; ﴿in mockery﴾; i.e., as objects of mockery, by turning away from them and being careless in observing what they contain of rulings and limits. This is from the expression said to someone who does not take a matter seriously: "You are jesting." It is as if it were a prohibition against mocking them, with what this entails of the opposite command intended: that is, be earnest in taking them up and acting by what they contain, and observe them with due observance; otherwise you have taken them as mockery and play. It is also permissible that what is meant is the prohibition against retaining for harm, since taking back without desire for her is, outwardly though not in reality, an act in accordance with the requirements of the signs of God, Exalted is He; and this is the meaning of mockery. It was said: a man would marry, divorce, and manumit, then say, "I was only joking," so this was revealed. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Three things are serious whether meant seriously or jokingly: marriage, divorce, and manumission."

﴿And remember the favour of God upon you﴾, in that He guided you to what brings your religious and worldly happiness; that is: respond to it with gratitude and by fulfilling its due rights. The adverbial phrase is connected to an omitted element that occurs as a circumstantial clause qualifying "the favour of God" — that is, "being upon you"; or it is a qualifier of it, according to the view of those who permit omitting the relative pronoun together with part of its clause, i.e., "that which is upon you." It is also permissible for it to be connected to the noun itself, if by it is meant the bestowal, since it is a verbal noun (ism masdar), like "nabat" from "anbata"; and the feminine ta' does not impair its governing, because it is built upon it, as in the verse:

﴿So were it not for the hope of help from you and fear of your punishment, they would have been to us like watering-places.﴾

﴿And what He sent down upon you﴾: a conjunction to "the favour of God"; "ma" is a relative pronoun, its returning pronoun having been omitted from the relative clause. The "min" in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿of the Book and wisdom﴾ is explicative (bayaniyya); that is: of the Qur'an and the Sunnah; or the Qur'an comprising both titles, the conjunction being for the difference of the two descriptions, as in the verse:

﴿To the sovereign lion and son of the noble one...﴾

The mention of it first in general terms and then specifying it carries a magnificence that is not hidden; and singling it out for mention, although it is the first thing that enters into the favour commanded to be remembered, shows its great importance and is an emphasis on urging observance of what was mentioned before it of rulings. ﴿He admonishes you through it﴾; i.e., through what He sent down; it is a circumstantial clause relating to the subject of "sent down" or its object, or to both together. ﴿And fear God﴾, regarding the matter of observing Him and fulfilling His obligatory rights. ﴿And know that God is knowing of all things﴾: nothing is hidden from Him of what you do and what you leave undone, so He will call you to account with its various kinds of punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 232:

﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them﴾: This is an explanation of the ruling concerning what they used to do when the term was actually reached, after explaining the ruling concerning what they used to do when it was approaching. Al-'adl (prevention) means confinement and restriction, and from it comes the expression "ʿaḍḍalati al-dajājatu" (the hen became egg-bound), when her egg has lodged and does not come out. The intended meaning is prohibition. The address is either to the guardians (awliya'), since it is reported that it was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar when he prevented his sister Jumal from returning to her former husband through marriage; and it is said that it was revealed concerning Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, when he prevented a paternal cousin of his. The attribution of the divorce to them is because they were the cause of it, as indicated by their taking the initiative in prevention. Perhaps the mention of reaching the term, although it is permissible to remarry the former husband before it, is because the aforementioned prevention occurs at that time. There is no indication in this that a woman may not marry herself; otherwise there would be no need to forbid the guardians from prevention, since the prohibition is to remove harm from them. For they, although they are able to marry themselves, refrain from doing so for fear of blame and severance. Or the address is to the husbands, since they used to prevent their divorcees and would not let them marry, out of oppression and compulsion, due to the zealotry of the Jahiliyya. Or the address is to people in general, for attributing to all what one of them did is common and widespread. The meaning is: when divorce occurs among you, let there be no prevention among you, whether it comes from the guardians, from the husbands, or from others. This includes an exaggeration of the matter of prevention and a warning against it, and an announcement that its occurrence among them while they remain silent about it is like its issuing from all of them in incurring blame and spreading harm. ﴿that they marry﴾: that is, from their marrying; its position is in the accusative according to Sibawayh and al-Farra', and in the genitive according to al-Khalil, according to the well-known difference of opinion. It is said that it is a badal al-ishtimal (substitute of inclusion) for the object pronoun in "ta'dulūhunna" (do not prevent them). In this is an indication of the validity of marriage by their own expression. ﴿their husbands﴾: if by them are meant the divorcers, then the marital relation is either by consideration of what was, or by consideration of what will be; otherwise, it is by the latter consideration. ﴿when they agree﴾: a temporal clause governing "lā taʿḍulū" (do not prevent). The masculine form is used by way of giving precedence to the address over the women. The restriction by it is because it is the customary case, not to permit prevention before the agreement is complete. It is said that it is a temporal clause governing "an yankiḥna" (that they marry). His words (exalted is He): ﴿between them﴾ is a temporal complement of the agreement, conveying its firmness and solidity. ﴿in a reasonable manner﴾: that is, what is good according to the Sharia and approved by people. The bā' (in) is either connected to an omitted element functioning as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "tarāḍaw" (they agreed), or as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: an agreement that is in accordance with what is reasonable; or it is connected to "tarāḍaw", meaning: they agree upon what is commendable in religion and manliness. In this is an implication that prevention from marrying a non-equal (kafu') or for less than the customary dower (mahr al-mithl) is not a case of prevention.

﴿That﴾: a reference to the rulings that have been detailed; and the notion of distance in it is for the glorification of the one referred to. The address is to all the obligated persons, as is the case in what follows. The singular form is either by consideration of each one of them, or by interpreting it as a group and a company, or because the kaf (you) is merely for address and to distinguish the present from the past, without specifying the addressees; or it refers to the Messenger (ﷺ), as in His words (exalted is He): ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾, to indicate that the reality of what is referred to is a matter that hardly anyone recognizes. ﴿With it is admonished whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾: so he hastens to comply with His commands and prohibitions, out of reverence for Him and fear of His punishment. His words (exalted is He): ﴿among you﴾ are either connected to "kāna" (was), according to those who permit its operation on adverbials and the like; or to an omitted element functioning as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "yu'minu" (believes), meaning: being among you. ﴿That﴾: that is, being admonished by it and acting upon its requirement. ﴿is purer for you﴾: that is, more conducive to growth and more beneficial, ﴿and more pure﴾ from the filth of sins and the defilement of transgressions. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what purity and cleanliness it contains; ﴿and you do not know﴾ that. Or: Allah knows what is good for your affairs of rulings and laws, of which this that He has explained here is part, and you do not know them; so leave your opinion and comply with His command and prohibition in everything you do and everything you leave undone.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 233:

﴿And the mothers shall suckle their children﴾: a beginning in explaining the rulings related to their children, specifically and generally. It is a matter expressed in the form of a report, for emphasis in driving toward the realization of its content. Its meaning is recommendation (nadb), or obligation (wujub) if it is restricted to the case of the child's refusal to take another's breast, or the absence of a wet-nurse (zi'r), or the father's inability to hire one. The expression of them by the mentioned title is to stir their compassion toward their children. The ruling is general for divorced women and others; and it has been said that it is specific to them, since the discussion concerns them. ﴿For two full years﴾: the emphasis by the attribute of completeness is to show that the period is a precise determination, not an approximate one, based on the customary leniency. ﴿For whoever wishes to complete the breastfeeding﴾: an explanation of who the ruling is directed at; that is, this applies to whoever wishes to complete the nursing. This indicates the permissibility of shortening it. It has also been said that the lam is connected to "yursi'na" (they suckle), since the father is obligated to arrange the nursing, like maintenance, and the mother nurses on his behalf, as one says: "So-and-so woman nursed so-and-so's child." ﴿And upon the one to whom the child is born﴾: that is, the father, for the child is born to him and attributed to him; the change of expression indicates the meaning that requires the obligation of nursing and the cost of the nursing mother upon him. ﴿Their provision and their clothing﴾: as a wage for them. There is disagreement regarding hiring the mother; it is not permissible according to us while she is in marriage or in the waiting period ('idda); it is permissible according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him. ﴿In a fair manner﴾: according to what the ruler sees fit, and what he can afford according to his capacity. ﴿No soul is burdened except according to its capacity﴾: a justification for the obligation of the maintenance in a fair manner, or an explanation of "fair manner." It is a text that God (exalted be He) does not burden the servant with what he cannot bear; and this does not contradict its possibility.

﴿No mother shall be harmed because of her child, nor a father because of his child﴾: a detailing of what precedes and a confirmation of it; that is, neither of them should burden the other with what they cannot bear, nor harm the other because of the child. It was read "lā tuḍārr" with a raised vowel, as a substitute for "tukallaf"; its original form in both readings is "lā tuḍārir" with a kasra, in the active voice, and with a fatha in the passive voice. On the first reading, it may mean "taḍurr" (to harm), with the bā' being part of its complement; that is, the parents should not harm the child, so that he is neglected in his care and falls short in what is due to him. It was also read "lā tuḍārr" with sukun and shadda, on the intention of pausing; and also with the light form, as from "ḍārahu, yaḍīruhu". The attribution of the child to each of them is to appeal to their compassion toward him, and to alert that he is deserving that both of them agree on his welfare, and that they should not harm him or harm each other through him. ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾: (p-231) a conjunction with His saying (exalted be He): ﴿and upon the one to whom the child is born, their provision﴾, etc. What lies between them is a justification or an intervening explanation. What is meant by it is the heir of the child, from among those who are a blood relative, a mahram of his; it has been said: his agnatic kin ('asaba). Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: "It is the heir of the father"; and it is the child; that is, the nursing mother is to be provided for from his property upon the death of the father; there is no dispute about this, and the discussion is only about the case in which the child has no property. It has also been said: it refers to the remaining of the two parents, from his statement, peace be upon him: "and make him the heir from us"; and that indicates what was obligatory upon the father, of provision and clothing. ﴿But if they both desire﴾; that is, the two parents; ﴿weaning﴾; that is, separation from nursing, before the completion of the two years; and the indefiniteness is to indicate that it is an unusual weaning. ﴿By mutual consent﴾: connected to an omitted element that the mind is led to; that is, issuing from mutual consent; ﴿from both of them﴾; that is, from the parents, not from only one of them, due to the possibility of one of them undertaking what harms the child, such as the woman becoming weary of nursing, and the father being stingy in giving the wage. ﴿And consultation﴾: regarding the child's affair, examining his conditions, and agreement between them that he deserves weaning. "Tashāwur" (consultation) derives from "mashūra", which is the extraction of an opinion, from "shurtu al-'asal" when you extracted the honey; and their indefiniteness is for magnification. ﴿Then there is no blame upon them both﴾: in that; because their mutual consent occurs only after their opinion has settled, or their effort has concluded that the child's welfare lies in weaning; and they rarely agree upon error. ﴿And if you desire﴾: an explanation of the ruling when they do not agree upon weaning; and the shift to addressing the fathers is to urge them to comply with what they were commanded. ﴿To seek wet-nurses for your children﴾; with the first object omitted, as it is unnecessary; that is, to seek wet-nurses for your children; one says: "The woman nursed the child" and "I sought a nurse for her to him." It has also been said: it transitively takes the second object by a prepositional particle; one says: "I sought a nurse of the woman for the child"; that is, to seek wet-nurses for your children; so the preposition was also omitted, as in His saying (exalted be He): ﴿and when they measure for them﴾; that is, measure for them. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you﴾; that is, in seeking a nurse; and this indicates that the father may seek a nurse for the child and prevent the mother from nursing. ﴿When you hand over﴾; that is, to the nurses; ﴿what you gave﴾; that is, what you intended to give, as in His saying (exalted be He): ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God﴾. It was read "mā ataytum", from "atā ilayhi iḥsānan" when he did it; and it was read "mā ūtītum", that is, from God's side (exalted and majestic is He), as in His saying (exalted be He): ﴿and spend of that in which He has made you successors﴾; and in it is an increased incitement for them to hand over. ﴿In a fair manner﴾: connected to "sallamtum"; that is, in the customary, legally commendable way; and the answer to the condition is omitted, due to what has been mentioned indicating it. Handing over is not a condition for validity or permissibility; rather, it is a recommendation toward what is most fitting and preferable, for when the nurses are given what has been determined for them immediately, hand to hand, that is more conducive to the welfare of the children's affairs. ﴿And fear God﴾: regarding observing the mentioned rulings; ﴿and know that God is Seeing of what you do﴾; so He will recompense you for that; and the manifestation of the noble Name in the place of the pronoun is to cultivate awe; and in it is a threat and warning that is not hidden.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 234:

﴿And those who﴾: this is by omitting an element that is added to (al-muḍāf, "the omitted noun"); that is, "and the wives of those who". ﴿are taken (in death) from among you﴾: that is, their souls are seized by death. For "al-tawaffī" (taking in full, here meaning death) is "al-qabḍ" (seizing). It is said: "I took back my money from so-and-so (tawaffaytu mālī min fulān)" and "I received it from him in full (istawfaytuhu minhu)", meaning I took it and seized it. The address is to all people, by way of "al-talwīn" (shifting the mode of address). ﴿and leave behind wives who shall wait by themselves for four months and ten (days)﴾. Or it is by omitting the pronoun referring back to the subject (al-mubtada', "the subject") in the predicate (al-khabar, "the predicate"), (p-232) that is: "shall wait after them", as in their saying: "Ghee is two manas for a dirham", meaning "two manas of it". It is also read as "yatawaffawna" with a fatha on the ya', meaning they receive their full terms (ājāl). The feminine form of "ashr" (ten) is due to considering the nights, because they are the cores (ghurar) of the months and days; for this reason you will hardly ever find them using the masculine form in such a case at all, to the extent that they say: "I fasted ten (ṣumtu ʿashran)". Clear evidence of this is His saying (exalted is He): ﴿You stayed only ten (days)﴾, then: ﴿You stayed only a day﴾. The wisdom in this determination is probably that if the fetus is male it usually moves after three months, and if it is female it moves after four, so the longer of the two terms was taken into account, and ten days were added to it as a precaution, since the movement may sometimes be weak so that it is not felt. The general wording requires that the Muslim woman, the Scripturist woman, the free woman and the slave woman be equal in this ruling; but analogy (al-qiyās) requires halving the term for the slave woman. His saying (mighty and majestic is He): ﴿and those who are pregnant﴾ singled out the pregnant woman from this. It is reported from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that she observes the longer of the two terms as a precaution. ﴿When they have reached their term﴾: that is, their waiting period (ʿidda) has ended. ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, O rulers and all Muslims, ﴿for what they do with themselves﴾, such as adorning themselves, exposing themselves to suitors, and all else that is forbidden to the woman observing the waiting period, ﴿in a fair manner﴾: in a manner which the Sharia does not disapprove of. This contains an indication that if they do what the Sharia disapproves of, then it is incumbent upon you to restrain them from that; otherwise, the blame falls upon you. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾: so do not act contrary to what you have been commanded.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 235:

﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾: an address to all. ﴿for what you hint at in [your] proposal﴾: "al-ta'ridh" (allusion) and "al-talwih" (hinting) mean obscuring the intended meaning by means of something that has not been set for it either literally or figuratively, such as the words of the one asking: "I have come to you so that I may greet you." Its origin is turning speech away from its straight course toward one of its sides ('urdh), that is, a side of it. Al-kinayah (metonymy) is indicating a thing by mentioning its concomitants and attendants, such as your saying "long of the sword-strap" for a tall man, and "abundant in ashes" for a generous host. ﴿from the proposal of women﴾: "al-khitbah" (proposal of marriage), with a kasra, like "al-qi'dah" and "al-jilsah" (sitting), is what the suitor does of request and courting, by word and by deed. It is said that it is derived from "al-khatb," that is, a matter of importance, since it is a matter among the matters and a kind of calamity. It is also said that it is derived from "al-khitab" (address), since it is a kind of address that takes place between the side of the man and the side of the woman. What is meant by "women" are those observing the waiting period for death. Allusion to their proposal is that he says to her: "Indeed you are beautiful," or "virtuous," or "beneficial," and "it is among my aims to marry," and the like, of what gives the impression that he wants to marry her, so that she may hold herself back for him if she is inclined toward him, and he does not state marriage explicitly. ﴿or you conceal within yourselves﴾: that is, you harbour in your hearts, without mentioning it explicitly or allusively. ﴿God knows that you will mention them﴾: and you will not be patient in keeping silent about them and in showing your desire for them. In this there is a kind of rebuke for them for their lack of deliberation. ﴿But do not make a promise to them in secret﴾: this is an exception from an omitted element indicated by "you will mention them," that is: so mention them, but do not promise them marriage; rather, be content with the allusion that has been permitted to you. The expression of marriage by "secret" is because its cause, which is intercourse, is something kept secret; choosing it over its name indicates that it is something that should be kept secret and concealed. Taking it to mean intercourse may perhaps suggest permission for what is forbidden, namely explicit mention of marriage. It is also said that "secretly" is an adverbial accusative of time, that is: do not promise them during the secret time, with the meaning that what is meant is promising something reprehensible; and there is much to be said about this. ﴿except that you say a fair word﴾: this is an exceptive construction without a complete antecedent, from what the prohibition implies, that is: do not promise them any promise except a known promise, not forbidden by the Sharia, which is what occurs by way of allusion and hinting; or: except a promise with a fair word; or: do not promise them anything except by saying a fair word. It is also said that it is a disjunctive exception from "secretly"; this is weak, because it leads to making allusion a promise, which it is not. ﴿And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾: from "'azama al-amr," when one intends it with firm intention; its real meaning is cutting off. The evidence is his saying ﷺ: "There is no fast for one who does not resolve to fast from the night," and it is narrated: "for one who does not make the fast a plan overnight." The prohibition of it is for emphasis in forbidding the actual undertaking of the marriage contract, that is: do not resolve to conclude the tie of marriage. ﴿until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾: that is, the prescribed waiting period, the appointed one, reaches its last part. It is also said that the meaning is: do not sever the tie of marriage, that is, do not finalise it, do not impose it, and do not proceed with it, so that it is a prohibition of the act itself, not of intending it. ﴿And know that God knows what is in your souls﴾: of what is in the breasts, of which resolving upon what you have been forbidden is part. ﴿so beware of Him﴾: by avoiding resolve from the outset, or by desisting from it after it has been established. ﴿And know that God is Forgiving﴾: He forgives whoever desists from his resolve out of fear of Him (exalted is He); ﴿Forbearing﴾: He does not hasten to punish you, so do not take His delay in punishment as evidence that what you have been forbidden of resolve is not something that entails accountability. The placing of the noble Name in the position of a pronoun is to bring in awe.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 236:

﴿There is no blame upon you﴾; that is: there is no liability for a dowry. This is the most apparent meaning. It was also said: (it means) no sin, since there is no innovation (bid'ah) in divorce before consummation (masis). It was also said: the Prophet (ﷺ) used to greatly forbid divorce, so it was thought that there was a sin in it, and so this was negated. ﴿If you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾; that is: as long as you have not had intercourse with them. It was read as "tumassuhunna" with a damma on the ta' in all positions; that is: for the duration of your not touching them. (This is) on the basis that "ma" is a temporal verbal particle (masdariyyah zarfiyyah), with an elided noun (taqdir al-mudaf). Abu al-Baqa' transmitted that it is conditional (shartiyyah), in the sense of "in" (if); then it would be an instance of a conditional clause interposed upon a conditional (i'tiraD al-shart 'ala al-shart), so the second becomes a restriction on the first, as in your saying: "If you come to me, if you do good to me, I will honour you"; that is: if you come to me doing good to me. The meaning is: if you divorce them while not having touched them. This meaning is more fitting than the first, because the temporal "ma" is appropriately used only when what is contained is an extended matter, coinciding with the duration or time attached to it, as in His (Exalted) saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾, and His (Exalted) saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾. It is not hidden that divorce is not like this; and attaching the temporal adverb to the negation of blame may give the impression that touching is possible after divorce. So the proper course is to take the circumstantial sense (hal) in place of the temporal and duration sense. ﴿Or you have appointed for them an obligation﴾; that is: except that you appoint for them (a dowry), or: until you appoint for them a dowry at the contract, on the basis that "fariydah" is "fa'ilah" in the sense of "maf'ul"; the ta' is for transferring the word from adjectival to nominal use; its accusative status is as an object. It may also be a verbal noun (masdar), in form and in grammatical function. The meaning is that there is no liability on the one who divorces for claiming the dowry at all, when the divorce is before consummation, in every case, except in the case of a named dowry, for then he is obligated to half of what was named. And in the case where it was not named, the obligation is the provision (mut'ah), half of the proper dowry (mahr al-mithl). As for when it is after consummation, then in the case of a named dowry he owes the full named amount, and in the case where none was named, the full proper dowry. It was also said: the word "aw" is coordinating, its complement conjoined to what precedes it of the jussive verb, in the sense: as long as there has been from you neither touching nor the appointing of a dowry. ﴿And provide for them﴾: a conjunction upon an implied element which the speech carries; that is: so divorce them, and provide for them. The wisdom in making provision obligatory is to remedy the distress of divorce, and it is: a shirt, a cloak, and a head-covering, according to circumstances, as His (Exalted) saying clarifies: ﴿The wealthy according to his means, and the straitened according to his means﴾; that is: what befits the condition of each of them. It was read with a sukun on the dal. It is a resumptive clause with no place in the grammatical structure, explaining the measure of the provision by considering the state of the one who divorces, in wealth and in straitness; or it is a circumstantial clause from the subject of "provide for them", with the connecting pronoun elided; that is: upon the wealthy among you... etc. Or, on the basis of making the alif and lam a substitute for the genitive complement, according to those who permit it; that is: upon your wealthy... etc. This applies when the proper dowry of such a woman is not less than that amount; if it is less, then she receives the lesser of half the proper dowry and the provision, and it must not fall below five dirhams. ﴿Provision﴾; that is: providing; ﴿in accordance with what is fair﴾; that is: in the manner which the Shari'ah and proper conduct (muru'ah) approve; ﴿as a duty﴾; an adjective of "provision", or an emphatic verbal noun; that is: this is due as a duty; ﴿upon the good-doers﴾; that is: those who do good to themselves by hastening to comply, or to the divorced women, by providing for them in a fitting manner. They were called "good-doers" by way of consideration of the participation and as encouragement and exhortation.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 237:

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you had already appointed for them a portion﴾; "before that" (qabla dhalika); "a portion" (fariḍatan), i.e.: and if you divorce them before touching (al-masis), while you had appointed for them, previously, i.e. at the marriage contract, a dower (mahr). The clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the subject of "you divorced them" (ṭallaqtumuhunna). It may also be a circumstantial clause relating to its object, to establish the connection (al-rābiṭ) with respect to both of them. The act of appointing (al-fard) may be in the active or the passive voice, even though it did not coincide with the time of divorce; for the description of the divorcer as one who had appointed (al-fāriḍiyya) previously is undoubtedly concurrent with it. Likewise the state of the divorced woman, being one for whom a portion had been appointed previously.

﴿then half of what you appointed﴾: i.e., then for them is half of what you specified for them of the dower; or: then it is obligatory upon you to pay that. This explicitly indicates that what is negated in the previous case is the liability for the dower. It has also been read in the accusative (naṣb), i.e.: then pay half of what you appointed. Perhaps the reason for delaying the ruling on specification, although it is the basic element in the contract and the more common occurrence, is that this noble verse was revealed concerning an Ansari man who married a woman from the Banu Hanifa, and she was one for whom no dower had been specified (mufawwaḍa). He divorced her before consummation, so they brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he (ﷺ) made clear that he owed nothing, he said to him: "Provide for her with your cap."

﴿except that they forgive﴾: an exceptive clause (istithnā' mufarragh) from the most general of circumstances; i.e., for them is half of what was appointed, specified, in every case, except in the case of their forgiveness, for then that is dropped after having become obligatory. The wording in itself allows both the masculine and the feminine readings; the distinction lies only in the grammatical analysis and verification: the waw in the first is a pronoun and the nun is the sign of the nominative, while in the second the lam is the verb's, the nun is a pronoun, and the verb is built accordingly. It has not affected it, in the way it affects what is conjoined to its place, from His (exalted) saying: ﴿or [that] he forgive﴾ in the accusative. It has also been read with the waw silent.

﴿or he in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾: i.e., the husband, who controls its contracting and its dissolution, leaves to her what would return to him of half the dower, which he had given her in full, as is customary, out of generosity. For abandoning his right against her is clearly a pardon. Or this is called a pardon in the case of non-delivery, by way of parallelism (mushākala); or by way of prevalence (taghlīb) of the state of delivery over the state of its absence. In that case the exception returns to forbidding an increase in the excepted part, just as in the first case it returns to forbidding a decrease in it; i.e., for them is this amount as an increase, with no decrease in any circumstance, except in the case of their forgiveness, for then they do not have the stated amount, but that is annulled or reduced; or in the case of the husband's forgiveness, for then they have an increase beyond that amount. This is according to the first interpretation. As for the second interpretation, it is necessary to take the exception as disjunctive (munqaṭi'), because in the case of the husband's forgiveness, an obligation upon him cannot be conceived. This is our position. In the older opinion of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, the intended meaning is the forgiveness of the guardian (walī) who holds the tie of marriage of a minor girl; and this is the apparent basis. However, the first is more suitable to His saying: ﴿And that you forgive is nearer to piety﴾, to its end, for dropping the right of a minor has nothing to do with piety.

It is reported from Jubayr ibn Mut'im that he married a woman and divorced her before consummation, and he completed the dower for her, and said: "I am more entitled to pardon." It has also been read with the yā' (i.e., "yaʿfū" with the letter yā'). ﴿And do not forget graciousness among you﴾: i.e., do not leave off that some of you show favour to others, as one would forget a thing; it has also been read with a kasra on the waw, and the address in both verbs is to men and women together by way of prevalence (taghlīb). ﴿Indeed Allah is seeing of what you do﴾: so He does not waste what you have done of favour and kindness.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 238:

﴿Guard the prayers,﴾ that is: persist in performing them at their appointed times, without neglecting any part of them; as is indicated by the form of the verb (ḥāfiẓū, from the pattern mufā'ala), which conveys emphasis. Perhaps the command to them, placed in the midst of the explanation of the rulings concerning spouses and children, before completing that discussion, is to notify that they (the prayers) deserve the utmost care regarding their status and perseverance in them, without being occupied with them (the family) to the neglect of them, but rather with regard to the self as well; as the command to perform them in a state of fear makes clear. For this reason it was commanded within the explanation of the rulings of the Sharia that concern them, which are intertwined, one holding onto the other. ﴿And the middle prayer﴾: that is, the one that lies between them (the other prayers), or: the most excellent of them. It is the ʿAṣr prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr), according to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb): "They have occupied us from the middle prayer, the ʿaṣr prayer; may Allah (Exalted) fill their houses and graves with fire." And he (ﷺ) said: "It is the prayer from which Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) was distracted." Its excellence is due to the great number of people occupied at its time with their trade and livelihoods, and the gathering of the angels of the night and the angels of the day at that time. It was also said: it is the Zuhr prayer, because it falls in the middle of the day, and it was the hardest of the prayers for them, since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform it at the time of intense heat (al-hājira), so it was the most excellent of them, according to his saying (ﷺ): "The most excellent acts of worship are the most arduous of them." It was also said: it is the Fajr prayer, because it lies between the prayers of the night and the day, falling on the shared boundary between them, and because it is witnessed, like the ʿaṣr prayer. It was also said: it is the Maghrib prayer, because it is in the middle in terms of number, and in terms of its occurrence between the daytime and nighttime prayers, and it is the odd (witr) prayer of the day, and it is not shortened during travel. It was also said: it is the ʿIsha prayer, because it lies between the two audible prayers that fall at the two ends of the night. It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "he (ﷺ) used to recite: 'And the middle prayer and the ʿaṣr prayer.'" In that case it is one of the four, singled out for mention together with ʿaṣr because of its distinctive excellence. It was also read: "wa-ʿalā al-ṣalāt al-wuṣṭā"; and it was read in the accusative, as a expression of praise; and it was read: "al-Wuṣṭā" (with ṣ). ﴿And stand before Allah﴾: that is, in the prayer; ﴿devoutly obedient (qānitīn)﴾: remembering Him (Exalted) while standing, because qunūt in it is the remembrance (dhikr) of Him; it was also said: it is the perfection of obedience and completing it without neglecting any of its pillars; it was also said: humbly submissive (khāshiʿīn). Ibn al-Musayyab said: what is meant by it is the qunūt in the Subh (Fajr) prayer.

(p-236) ﴿Then if you fear﴾: that is, from an enemy or otherwise; ﴿on foot﴾: the plural of "rājil" (pedestrian), like "qiyām" and "qā'im"; or "rajul" in the sense of "rājil." It is also read with a ḍamma on the rā' with light pronunciation, and with a ḍamma and shadda as well. It is also read "farajulan," meaning "rājilan" (on foot). ﴿or riding﴾: the plural of "rākib" (rider); that is, "pray on foot or riding, as the situation requires, and do not neglect the prayer as long as it is possible to stand in general." Al-Shāfi'ī, may Allah have mercy on him, permitted performing it even while fighting hand-to-hand. ﴿Then when you are secure﴾: with the removal of fear; ﴿then remember Allah﴾: that is, pray the prayer of security. It was expressed by "remembrance" because it is the greatest of its pillars. ﴿as He taught you﴾: this is connected to a omitted verb that occurs as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun; that is, a remembrance that is as He taught you; that is, like His teaching you. ﴿what you did not used to know﴾: concerning the manner of the prayer. The intended meaning of the comparison is that the prayer performed should conform to what Allah (Exalted) taught. Its mention under this heading serves to remind of the blessing. Or: give thanks to Allah (Exalted) with a thanks that matches His teaching you what you did not know of the laws and rulings, among which is the manner of establishing the prayer in the states of fear and security. This is it. And in the introduction of the first conditional with the word "in," which indicates the uncertainty of the occurrence of fear and its rarity, and the opening of the second conditional with the word "idhā," which signals the certainty of the occurrence of security and its frequency; together with brevity in the answer to the first and elaboration in the answer to the second, both based on treating the situation in which the commanded act occurs in each of them as the situation of the command's occurrence, a treatment that calls for applying to each of them the requirement of the second situation, with the eloquence and subtlety of consideration it contains, as a lesson for those of insight.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 240:

﴿And those of you who are taken in death and leave wives behind﴾: This is a return to explaining the remaining detailed rulings mentioned earlier, after rulings were placed between them, because of the wisdom that was pointed out as calling for that. ﴿A bequest for their wives﴾: that is, they should bequeath; or: let them bequeath; or: God (exalted is He) prescribed for them a bequest. What supports this is the reading of the one who recited "a bequest is prescribed for you, for your wives." It was also read in the nominative, by supposing a noun to be omitted in the subject or in the predicate, meaning: "The ruling concerning those of you who are taken in death and leave wives is a bequest for their wives"; or: "Those who are taken in death are people of a bequest for their wives"; or: "a bequest is prescribed for them"; or: "a bequest is upon them." It was also read: "provision (matā') for their wives" in place of "a bequest." ﴿Provision until the year's end﴾: it is in the accusative governed by "they bequeath," if you supply it; otherwise by "the bequest," or, on the last reading, by "provision." ﴿Without expulsion﴾: it is a substitute for it; or an emphatic verbal noun, as in your saying, "This statement is other than what you say"; or a circumstantial clause referring to "their wives," meaning: not expelled. The meaning: it is obligatory upon those of you who are taken in death to bequeath, before the approach of death, for their wives to be provided for after them for a year, with maintenance and lodging. This was at the beginning of Islam. Then the period was abrogated (naskh) by His saying (exalted is He): ﴿four months and ten days﴾. For it, although it precedes in recitation, came later in revelation. The maintenance was dropped by her inheriting a quarter or an eighth. Likewise the lodging according to us; according to al-Shafi'i it remains. ﴿But if they leave﴾: from the husbands' dwelling by their own choice. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you﴾, O guardians (al-a'immah), ﴿concerning what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾: what the Sharia does not reject, such as adorning themselves, perfuming, abandoning mourning, and exposing themselves to suitors. This indicates that what is forbidden is their leaving when they wish to remain, and keeping to the husband's dwelling and mourning, without this being obligatory upon them (p-237), and that they were given the choice between staying with the maintenance and leaving while forgoing it. ﴿And God is Mighty﴾: dominant over His command, punishing whoever opposes Him; ﴿Wise﴾: He considers the interests of His servants in His rulings.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 241:

﴿And for the divorced women﴾: whether they have been consummated with or not; ﴿a provision﴾, i.e., an absolute provision (mut'ah), encompassing both the obligatory (wajibah) and the recommended (mustahabbah). Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Zuhri held that it is obligatory for all. It was also said: the meaning of "provision" (mata') is the maintenance during the waiting period ('iddah). It was also said: the lam (in lil-mutallaqat) is for a specific reference (lil-'ahd), and the intended women are those not yet consummated; and the repetition (of the statement) is for emphasis. ﴿In a fair manner﴾, according to the Sharia and custom. ﴿A duty upon the God-conscious﴾; i.e., from that which is not to be disregarded.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 242:

﴿Thus﴾; that is, like that clear exposition; ﴿Allah makes His signs clear to you﴾; which indicate His rulings, which He has legislated for His servants; ﴿so that you may understand﴾; so that you may comprehend what is in them, and act in accordance with their requirements.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 243:

﴿Have you not seen?﴾: This is an affirmation addressed to whoever has heard their story from the People of the Book and the narrators of reports, and an expression of wonder at their remarkable condition. Their hearing of it is equivalent to theoretical or cognitive sight. Or it is addressed to everyone who has a share in the address, as a notification that their story is so famous and widespread that it is right for everyone to be taken to acknowledge having seen them and heard their story, and to be amazed by it, even if he did not see them or hear their story. This expression has become like a proverb in the context of wonder, because it likens the state of one who did not see a marvelous thing to the state of one who saw it, on the basis of the claim that its matter is manifest and clear, such that both the present and the absent are equal in perceiving it. Then the speech is directed to him as it is directed to the one who saw, intending to exaggerate its fame and its distinction in wonder. The verb "see" is followed by "to" in His saying (exalted is He): ﴿to those who went out of their homes﴾, on the assumption that it means sight in the sense of looking, and on the assumption that it is inner perception, by implication of the meaning of reaching and arriving, in the sense of: "Has your knowledge not reached them?"

﴿while they were thousands﴾: that is, many thousands. It was said: ten thousand. It was said: thirty thousand. It was said: seventy thousand. The clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "went out".

His saying (mighty and majestic is He): ﴿fearing death﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu). It is narrated that the people of Dawardan, a village before Wasit, were struck by the plague, so they went out from it fleeing, and God (exalted is He) caused them to die, then revived them, so that they would take warning and know that there is no escape from the decree of God, mighty is His authority, and His judgment. It was also said: Ezekiel (Ḥizqīl) passed by them after a long time, and their bones were bare and their joints had come apart; so he twisted his cheeks and his fingers in wonder at what he saw of their condition. Then it was revealed to him: "Call out to them: Rise by God's leave." So he called out, and behold, they were standing, saying: "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You; there is no god but You." It was also said: they were a people from the Children of Israel whom their king called to jihad, so they fled, fearing death, and God (exalted is He) caused them to die for eight days, then revived them.

His saying (mighty and majestic is He): ﴿So God said to them: Die﴾ is either an expression of the connection of His will (exalted is He) to their death at once, or an figure for His causing them to die with the death of a single soul, in the nearest and least time, and the swiftest span of time, and by the command of one obeyed, to one obedient, as in His saying (exalted is He): (p-238) ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

﴿Then He revived them﴾: a conjunction, either upon an implied element demanded by the context, meaning: "So they died, then He revived them." It was omitted to indicate that it is dispensable to mention it, because it is impossible for His purpose (exalted is He) to differ from His will. Or it is upon "said", since it is an expression for causing death. In this there is encouragement for the Muslims to fight in jihad and to seek the causes of martyrdom, and that since death is unavoidable and flight from it does not benefit, it is more fitting that it be in the way of God (exalted is He).

﴿Indeed, God is truly full of bounty﴾, great, ﴿toward mankind﴾ entirely. As for those people, He revived them so that they would take warning from what befell them, and thus attain the greatest happiness; and as for those who heard their story, He guided them to the path of reflection and insight. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾: that is, they do not give thanks for His bounty as it should be given. It is permissible that by thanks is meant reflection and insight, and the placing of "mankind" in the position of the pronoun is for the sake of greater condemnation.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 244:

﴿And fight in the way of Allah﴾: it is a conjunction (ʿatf) over an implied element (muqaddar), which the preceding context specifies, as if it were said: "Be thankful for His bounty by taking heed of what He has related to you; and fight in His way, for you know that flight does not save one from death, and that what has been decreed cannot be averted. So if the term has come, then it is death in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if not, then it is a mighty victory and reward." ﴿And know that Allah is Hearing﴾: He hears the speech of those who went before and of those who stayed behind; ﴿Knowing﴾: of what they conceal within themselves; and He is beyond the recompense, good and evil. So hasten to comply, and beware of opposition and negligence.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 245:

﴿Who is it that will lend Allah⁠⁠ ﴾: "Man" is interrogative; it is in the nominative case of place by virtue of being the subject (mubtada'); "dha" is its predicate (khabar); and the relative clause is a qualifier (sifah) of it, or a substitute (badal) for it. The lending to Allah (Exalted is He) is a metaphor for presenting a deed that yields immediate benefit in pursuit of a reward that is deferred. What is meant here is either jihad, which is an expression for giving up one's self and wealth in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, seeking His good pleasure; or it is any righteous deed in general, which encompasses it in a primary sense. ﴿A goodly loan﴾: that is, a lending accompanied by sincerity and a contented soul; or: a loan that is lawful and good. ﴿So that He may multiply it for him﴾: in the accusative case, as a response to the interrogative, taking the meaning into account, since it is in the sense of "Will He lend to him?"; it has also been read in the nominative, meaning: He multiplies his reward and his recompense. This was made a multiplication of it on the basis of the apparent connection between them through causation and being caused. The form of the verb (mufa'alah) is for emphasis. It has also been read as "fayud'ifahu," both in the nominative and the accusative. ﴿Manifold﴾: the plural of "di'f" (double), and its accusative is either as a circumstantial state (hal) of the object pronoun, or as a direct object (maf'ul) by implying that "multiplying" carries the sense of "making," or as an emphatic infinitive (masdar), on the basis that "da'f" is a noun for the infinitive, and the plural form is due to the tanwin. ﴿Many﴾: none knows its measure except Allah (Exalted is He). It was said: one becomes seven hundred. ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾: that is, He restricts for some and widens for others; or: He restricts at times and widens at others, as His will dictates, which is founded upon wisdoms and interests. So do not be stingy towards Him with what He has extended to you, lest He change your circumstances. The mention of extending after withholding in the wording may be a hint that it follows it in existence, as a consolation to the poor. It has been read as "yabsut" with the sad, due to the proximity of the ta'. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: so He will recompense you for the deeds you have sent forward, good and bad.(p-239)

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 2, verse 246:

﴿Have you not considered?﴾: a confirmation and an expression of wonder, as has preceded. It is detached from what came before to signal that it stands independently in wonder, although it has a greater connection to what was placed between them, the command to fight. ﴿To the chiefs (al-mala') of the Children of Israel﴾. Al-mala' of a people are their faces (wujuh) and their nobles (ashraf). It is a collective noun with no singular from its own root, like "al-rahs" and "al-qawm." They were so called because they fill the eyes with awe and gatherings with splendor, or because they are "full" (maliyyun) of what is sought from them. The "min" here is partitive (tab'idiyyah). The "min" in His (exalted) words ﴿after Musa﴾ is for the starting point (ibtida'iyyah), and its governing element is implied, and it occurs as a circumstantial clause (hal) from "al-mala'," meaning: being some of the Children of Israel, after the death of Musa. There is no harm in the two particles being identical in form when their meanings differ. ﴿When they said﴾: it is governed by an implied element that the context requires, meaning: have you not considered the story of the chiefs, or their account, when they said: ﴿to a prophet of theirs﴾. He is Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Afra'im ibn Yusuf, peace be upon them both. It was also said: Shem'un ibn Sab'ah ibn 'Alqamah, from the descendants of Lawi ibn Ya'qub, peace be upon them both. It was also said: Ashmawil ibn Bal ibn 'Alqamah, which in Hebrew is "Isma'il." Muqatil said: he is from the offspring of Harun, peace be upon him. Mujahid said: Ashmawil ibn Hilqaya. ﴿Raise up for us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah﴾: that is, rise up to fight with us under a commander who issues decisions in the management of war according to his own judgment. It was read "nuqatilu" in the nominative, as a presumed circumstantial clause, meaning: raise him up for us as those who intend to fight; or as a resumptive clause built on a question. It was read "yuqatil" with the yā' and in the jussive and nominative, as a response to the imperative and as a description of "malikan." He said: It is a resumptive clause, coming as an answer to a question that the mind is led to, as if it were said: "What did the prophet say to them at that time?"
